To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
2-year-olds have a verb-general knowledge of argument structure and semantic roles for transitive structures, but they do not have verb-general knowledge until age 3;4 for intransitive structures.
English-learning children can associate transitive structure with causal events from 2;2 and can use transitives to correctly assign agent and patient from 2;4.
children aged 2 are able to associate transitive structures (e.g., John kicked the ball) with externally caused events and can assign agent and patient semantic roles to these structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the acquisition of argument structure and the assignment of semantic roles to arguments.
the development of children's comprehension of argument structure and semantic role assignment.
the development of children's knowledge of argument structure, and in particular, the development of children’s knowledge of semantic roles and their association with argument structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the comprehension of the conjoined-agent intransitive structure is not fully developed until the age of 3;4, and that the comprehension of transitive structure is fully developed before the age of 2.
children aged 2;6 can comprehend transitive argument structure and semantic roles and children aged 3;6 can comprehend intransitive argument and semantic roles.
the acquisition of argument structure is a gradual and piecemeal process, with the acquisition of transitive structures preceding the acquisition of conjoined agent in transitive structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
children are able to understand transitive argument structure at an earlier age than they can understand intransitive argument structures.

the children were able to understand the causal structure of events and to use this knowledge to map transitive structures to events, but that they had not developed the ability to use the same knowledge to understand intransitive structures until 3;4 years of age.
the children in this study had knowledge of transitive and in-transitive structure and the semantic roles assigned to them by age two, and that this knowledge was verb-general.

children's comprehension of argument structure and semantic roles can be investigated with a simple and efficient paradigm that does not rely on infants' looking behavior.
